name: Searched augmentation policies
positive_test: selects which augmentations to apply by searching over policies against a validation signal
negative_test: a fixed augmentation list chosen by hand
examples: AutoAugment, Fast AutoAugment, RandAugment, TrivialAugment, PBA
notes: sits on two axes at once by construction

name: Adversarial example generation
positive_test: constructs an input perturbation that maximises the model's loss under a norm budget
negative_test: random noise with no maximisation step
examples: FGSM, PGD, C&W, AutoAttack
notes: same procedure serves as attack and as training-data source

name: Learned-model tree search
positive_test: combines a learned model with an explicit tree search that produces the acting policy
negative_test: planning by trajectory sampling without a tree
examples: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, MuZero, EfficientZero, Sampled MuZero
notes: the clearest case of one lineage spanning two roles

name: Preference-based alignment
characteristic: whether a reward model is fit, and how the policy is updated against preferences
positive_test: optimises a policy against pairwise or ranked human or AI preference judgements
negative_test: optimising against a scalar reward supplied by the environment
examples: RLHF, DPO, GRPO-with-reward-model

name: Reward modelling plus policy optimisation
positive_test: fits an explicit reward model on comparisons, then runs an RL algorithm against it
negative_test: optimising the policy on preferences in closed form, with no reward model
examples: RLHF with PPO, RLAIF, Constitutional AI, reward-model ensembles

name: Direct preference optimisation
positive_test: derives a closed-form policy loss from the preference pairs, skipping the reward model
examples: DPO, IPO, KTO, ORPO, SimPO, cDPO, CPO

name: Rejection-sampled finetuning
positive_test: samples candidates, keeps the best by a scorer, then does supervised finetuning on them
examples: best-of-n finetuning, RAFT, STaR, rejection-sampling SFT, ReST
notes: sits between SFT and RL

name: Verifier-rewarded RL
positive_test: the reward comes from a programmatic checker rather than a learned or human judgement
negative_test: a reward model trained on human comparisons
examples: RLVR, unit-test reward, math-answer-match reward

name: Label-aware contrastive learning
positive_test: treats all same-class examples as positives using ground-truth labels
negative_test: treating only augmented views of one instance as positives
examples: SupCon, contrastive representation distillation

name: Guidance of the diffusion trajectory
positive_test: steers sampling with an external or implicit conditional signal during generation
negative_test: conditioning only through the training objective
examples: classifier guidance, classifier-free guidance, ControlNet conditioning, CFG rescaling
notes: role is decoding although the lineage is generative

name: Diffusion samplers and distillation
positive_test: reduces the number of denoising steps needed to produce a sample
negative_test: the training procedure that fits the denoiser
examples: DDIM, DPM-Solver, UniPC, progressive distillation, consistency models, LCM
notes: lineage drifts from objective to decoder; see Tensions

name: Scaling-rule hyperparameter transfer
positive_test: sets step sizes by a width or compute scaling law transferred from a smaller model
negative_test: tuning the step size on the target model directly
examples: muP, muTransfer, linear batch-size scaling rule, square-root scaling

name: Domain adaptation and invariance
characteristic: what quantity is aligned across domains
positive_test: trains with data from a source domain to perform on a shifted target domain
negative_test: adapting after deployment with no training-time target data
examples: DANN, CORAL, IRM

name: Adversarial domain alignment
positive_test: trains a domain discriminator the feature extractor is trained to fool
negative_test: matching moments or kernels in closed form
examples: DANN, ADDA, CDAN, MDD

name: Statistic-matching alignment
positive_test: minimises an explicit discrepancy between source and target feature statistics
examples: CORAL, Deep CORAL, MMD/DAN, JAN, optimal-transport alignment

name: Invariant risk and environment-based objectives
positive_test: requires the optimal predictor to be simultaneously optimal across labelled environments
examples: IRM, REx, GroupDRO, Fish, CLOvE

name: Distributional and adversarial robustness
characteristic: what adversary the objective is minimised against
positive_test: minimises a worst-case rather than an average risk
examples: DRO, PGD adversarial training, randomised smoothing

name: Distributionally robust optimisation
positive_test: minimises the worst-case loss over a set of reweightings of the training distribution
negative_test: minimising worst case over input perturbations
examples: DRO, CVaR-DRO, GroupDRO, chi-square DRO

name: Adversarial training
positive_test: solves an inner maximisation over input perturbations inside each training step
negative_test: perturbing inputs without maximising the loss
examples: PGD adversarial training, TRADES, MART, FastAT, free adversarial training

name: Certified robustness
positive_test: returns a provable guarantee of invariance within a stated input region
examples: randomised smoothing, IBP, CROWN, convex relaxations

name: Meta-learning
characteristic: what quantity is meta-learned
positive_test: optimises across a distribution of tasks so that per-task adaptation is cheap
negative_test: training on one task distribution with no inner adaptation loop
examples: MAML, prototypical networks, RL-squared

name: Optimisation-based meta-learning
positive_test: meta-learns an initialisation whose few-step adaptation performs well
negative_test: meta-learning a metric or a black-box update
examples: MAML, FOMAML, Reptile, ANIL, Meta-SGD, iMAML

name: Metric-based few-shot learning
positive_test: classifies by distance to class representatives in a learned embedding
examples: Siamese networks, Matching Networks, Prototypical Networks, Relation Networks

name: Black-box and in-context adaptation
positive_test: adaptation happens in activations or recurrent state, with no parameter update
negative_test: adapting by gradient steps at task time
examples: RL-squared, SNAIL, in-context learning as meta-learning
notes: partly speculative as a *training* procedure

name: Learned optimisers
positive_test: meta-trains a parametric update rule applied to another model's parameters
examples: learning to learn by gradient descent, VeLO, L2O
notes: the learned optimiser is a model; the meta-training is the algorithm

name: Continual learning
characteristic: how interference with earlier tasks is resisted
positive_test: trains on a sequence of tasks without full access to earlier data
examples: EWC, A-GEM, iCaRL

name: Importance-weighted parameter anchoring
positive_test: penalises movement of parameters deemed important to earlier tasks
examples: EWC, SI, MAS, Riemannian walk

name: Rehearsal
positive_test: stores or regenerates earlier examples and mixes them into current training
negative_test: constraining parameters without any stored data
examples: experience replay, GEM, A-GEM, DER, iCaRL, generative replay

name: Capacity isolation
positive_test: allocates disjoint parameters or masks per task
examples: progressive networks, PackNet, HAT, supermasks

name: Gradient projection
positive_test: projects updates onto directions that do not disturb earlier-task outputs
examples: orthogonal gradient descent, GPM, Adam-NSCL

name: Parameter-efficient adaptation
characteristic: where the new degrees of freedom live
positive_test: adapts a pretrained model while updating only a small fraction of, or an addition to, its parameters
negative_test: updating every parameter of the pretrained model
examples: LoRA, adapters, prefix tuning, BitFit

name: Inserted adapter modules
positive_test: inserts new trainable submodules into the frozen network and trains only those
examples: Houlsby adapters, Pfeiffer adapters, AdapterFusion, Compacter, Parallel adapters

name: Low-rank weight reparameterisation
positive_test: adds a trainable low-rank update to existing weight matrices, mergeable at inference
negative_test: adding modules that change the computation graph at inference
examples: LoRA, QLoRA, AdaLoRA, DoRA, LoRA+, ReLoRA, VeRA

name: Prompt and prefix tuning
positive_test: trains continuous vectors prepended to the input or to the attention keys and values
examples: prefix tuning, prompt tuning, P-tuning v2, soft prompts

name: Sparse parameter selection
positive_test: trains a chosen sparse subset of the existing parameters
negative_test: adding new parameters of any kind
examples: BitFit, IA3, diff pruning, Fish-Mask, surgical finetuning

name: Freezing and staged unfreezing
positive_test: holds some existing layers fixed and trains the rest, with no new parameters beyond a head
negative_test: training all layers from the first step
examples: linear probing, feature extraction, gradual unfreezing, ULMFiT schedule, LP-FT

name: Supervised adaptation recipes
characteristic: what the demonstration data is and how it is composed
positive_test: finetunes a pretrained model on labelled demonstrations of the target behaviour
examples: BERT finetuning, FLAN, Alpaca-style SFT

name: Instruction tuning
positive_test: finetunes on instruction-response pairs across many tasks to induce instruction following
negative_test: finetuning on a single downstream task
examples: FLAN, T0, Natural Instructions, Alpaca, Tulu-style SFT

name: Single-task finetuning
positive_test: adapts a pretrained model to one labelled downstream task
examples: BERT finetuning, ULMFiT, task-specific heads

name: Hyperparameter optimisation
characteristic: how the next configuration is chosen
positive_test: runs multiple training trials to select hyperparameters by a validation signal
negative_test: picking hyperparameters by hand or by citation
examples: grid search, TPE, Hyperband, PBT

name: Enumerative and random search
positive_test: draws configurations from a fixed design with no adaptation to past trials
negative_test: choosing the next point from previous results
examples: grid search, random search, Sobol/quasi-random, Latin hypercube
notes: random search is the baseline everyone must beat

name: Surrogate-model search
positive_test: fits a probabilistic surrogate to past trials and maximises an acquisition function
negative_test: allocating budget without modelling the response surface
examples: GP-EI Bayesian optimisation, TPE, SMAC, BOHB, BORE

name: Budget-allocation search
positive_test: reallocates compute across running trials by early-stopping the weak ones
examples: successive halving, Hyperband, ASHA, BOHB, PBT

name: Gradient-based hyperparameter optimisation
positive_test: differentiates a validation loss with respect to hyperparameters
negative_test: treating the trial as a black box
examples: hypergradient descent, implicit differentiation, DARTS-style relaxation

name: Transferred and predicted configurations
positive_test: sets hyperparameters from a scaling rule or a meta-model, without search on the target
negative_test: searching directly at the target scale
examples: muTransfer, meta-learned priors, scaling-law extrapolation, zero-shot HPO

name: Neural architecture search
characteristic: how the architecture space is traversed
positive_test: searches over architectures using a measured or predicted performance signal
examples: NASNet, DARTS, Once-for-All
notes: the product is a model; the search is the algorithm

name: Controller-based search
positive_test: trains a controller policy that emits architectures, rewarded by their accuracy
negative_test: mutating a population or relaxing the space
examples: NASNet/Zoph-Le, ENAS, MetaQNN

name: Evolutionary architecture search
positive_test: mutates and selects architectures in a population
negative_test: following a gradient through architecture weights
examples: AmoebaNet/regularised evolution, NEAT, hierarchical evolution

name: Differentiable architecture search
positive_test: relaxes discrete choices into continuous weights and follows their gradient
examples: DARTS, PC-DARTS, GDAS, ProxylessNAS, SNAS

name: Supernet and weight-sharing search
positive_test: trains one over-parameterised network whose subnetworks are the candidates
examples: one-shot NAS, Once-for-All, BigNAS, SPOS

name: Training-free architecture scoring
positive_test: ranks architectures by a proxy computable without training
examples: zero-cost proxies, NASWOT, synflow score

name: Pipeline and algorithm selection
characteristic: what part of the pipeline is searched
positive_test: searches jointly over preprocessing, model family and hyperparameters
negative_test: searching hyperparameters of a fixed model family
examples: Auto-WEKA, auto-sklearn, TPOT, AutoGluon, H2O AutoML

name: Pruning
characteristic: what score decides which parameters are removed
positive_test: sets a subset of parameters to zero and removes them from the computation
negative_test: lowering the numeric precision of all parameters
examples: magnitude pruning, lottery ticket, SparseGPT

name: Curvature-based saliency pruning
positive_test: scores parameters by an estimated loss increase from removing them
examples: OBD, OBS, WoodFisher, SNIP, GraSP

name: Magnitude and movement pruning
positive_test: removes the smallest weights, or those moving toward zero during finetuning
examples: magnitude pruning, iterative magnitude pruning, lottery ticket, movement pruning, RigL

name: Structured pruning
positive_test: removes whole channels, heads, layers or structured blocks
examples: channel pruning, head pruning, LLM-Pruner, 2:4 structured sparsity, ShortGPT

name: One-shot post-training pruning
positive_test: prunes a trained model using a small calibration set and a local reconstruction
negative_test: pruning during training with retraining between steps
examples: SparseGPT, Wanda, Optimal BERT Surgeon

name: Quantization
characteristic: whether and how the network is retrained to the quantized grid
positive_test: reduces the numeric precision of weights or activations
examples: GPTQ, LSQ, BinaryConnect

name: Post-training quantization
positive_test: quantises a finished model using only a small calibration set, with no gradient training
negative_test: training the model with quantization in the loop
examples: min-max calibration, GPTQ, AWQ, SmoothQuant, LLM.int8, QuIP, SpQR

name: Quantization-aware training
positive_test: simulates quantization in the forward pass and trains through a straight-through estimator
examples: QAT, LSQ, PACT, DoReFa

name: Binarisation and ternarisation
positive_test: reduces weights or activations to one or two bits
examples: BinaryConnect, XNOR-Net, BNN, TWN

name: Inference-cache quantization
positive_test: quantises the attention cache rather than the parameters
examples: KV-cache quantization, KIVI, per-channel cache scaling

name: Knowledge distillation
characteristic: what of the teacher is matched
positive_test: trains a student against targets produced by a teacher model
examples: Hinton KD, FitNets, DistilBERT
notes: role is objective; compression is a goal, not a slot

name: Output-distribution distillation
positive_test: matches the teacher's softened output distribution
examples: Hinton KD, born-again networks, DistilBERT, decoupled KD, sequence-level KD

name: Representation distillation
positive_test: matches internal activations, attention maps or relations
examples: FitNets, attention transfer, CRD, relational KD, TinyBERT

name: Self-distillation
positive_test: teacher and student are the same architecture, or the model's own earlier state
examples: born-again networks, self-distillation, BAN, deep mutual learning

name: Weight factorisation
characteristic: which decomposition is applied
positive_test: replaces a weight tensor with a product of smaller factors
negative_test: zeroing or requantising the original tensor
examples: SVD compression, Tucker decomposition, CP decomposition, ASVD
notes: speculative: often reported without a name

name: Sequence decoding
characteristic: how the next output is chosen from the model's scores
positive_test: converts the model's scores into an emitted sequence at inference time
examples: beam search, nucleus sampling, speculative decoding
notes: decides what is selected, so it decides what the model says

name: Greedy decoding
positive_test: emits the argmax at every step with no lookahead and no sampling
examples: greedy decoding, argmax decoding

name: Beam search
positive_test: maintains a fixed number of partial hypotheses ranked by cumulative score
negative_test: keeping only one hypothesis, or sampling
examples: beam search, length-normalised beam, diverse beam search, constrained beam search

name: Truncated stochastic sampling
positive_test: samples from the output distribution after reshaping or truncating its tail
examples: ancestral sampling, temperature, top-k, nucleus/top-p, typical sampling, min-p, eta sampling, Mirostat

name: Contrastive decoding
positive_test: scores a token by the difference between two models' or two layers' log-probabilities
examples: contrastive decoding, DoLa, context-aware decoding, contrastive search

name: Constrained decoding
positive_test: masks tokens that would violate a grammar, schema or lexical constraint
examples: grammar-constrained decoding, FSM-constrained decoding, lexically constrained decoding, JSON-schema decoding

name: Candidate reranking and MBR
positive_test: generates a candidate set and selects among complete candidates by a utility
examples: MBR decoding, reranking by model score, n-best reranking, quality-estimation reranking

name: Speculative decoding
positive_test: a cheap proposer drafts tokens that the target model verifies in parallel
negative_test: a single model emitting one token per forward pass
examples: speculative decoding, Medusa, EAGLE, lookahead decoding, self-speculative decoding
notes: changes cost, not the output distribution

name: Guided generation
positive_test: perturbs the output distribution with an auxiliary scorer or an unconditional contrast
examples: classifier guidance, classifier-free guidance, PPLM, FUDGE, GeDi
notes: shared with the diffusion lineage

name: Test-time search and deliberation
characteristic: what structure the search explores
positive_test: spends extra inference compute exploring multiple reasoning or action paths
negative_test: a single forward pass per output
examples: self-consistency, tree of thoughts, MCTS

name: Sample-and-select
positive_test: samples several complete attempts and selects or aggregates among them
examples: best-of-n, self-consistency majority vote, weighted best-of-n, rejection sampling at inference

name: Structured reasoning search
positive_test: expands and scores partial reasoning states in a tree or graph
examples: chain-of-thought prompting, least-to-most, tree of thoughts, graph of thoughts, PRM-guided beam, MCTS-guided decoding
notes: CoT is a named procedure, so it is admissible

name: Iterative refinement loops
positive_test: re-invokes the model on its own previous output plus feedback, in a loop
negative_test: a single generation with no revision
examples: ReAct, Reflexion, self-refine, self-debug, multi-agent debate

name: Explicit planning over a model
positive_test: searches over an environment or dynamics model to choose an action
negative_test: choosing an action by a direct policy forward pass
examples: A-star, Dijkstra, MCTS, UCT, PUCT, CEM-MPC, MPPI, iLQR, DDP
notes: shared with model-based RL

name: Retrieval and context construction
characteristic: how candidate context is scored
positive_test: selects external items to place in the model's input at inference
examples: BM25, DPR, RAG

name: Lexical retrieval
positive_test: scores documents by weighted term overlap with the query
examples: TF-IDF, BM25, BM25+, SPLADE (hybrid)

name: Learned dense retrieval
positive_test: scores by inner product of learned query and document embeddings
examples: DSSM, DPR, ANCE, ColBERT, E5, GTE
notes: trained contrastively, used at inference

name: Approximate nearest-neighbour search
positive_test: finds approximate nearest neighbours under an index structure with a recall-speed trade-off
examples: LSH, IVF-PQ, HNSW, DiskANN, ScaNN

name: Retrieval-augmented generation
positive_test: conditions generation on retrieved passages, possibly trained jointly
negative_test: retrieving without feeding the result to a generator
examples: kNN-LM, REALM, RAG, FiD, RETRO, Self-RAG

name: Retrieval reranking and fusion
positive_test: re-scores or merges candidate lists from a first-stage retriever
examples: cross-encoder reranking, monoT5, reciprocal rank fusion, ColBERT late interaction

name: Calibration and uncertainty quantification
characteristic: what produces the uncertainty estimate
positive_test: converts model outputs into calibrated probabilities, intervals or abstentions
examples: temperature scaling, conformal prediction, deep ensembles

name: Post-hoc probability recalibration
positive_test: fits a small mapping from scores to probabilities on a held-out split
negative_test: producing uncertainty from multiple models or a posterior
examples: Platt scaling, isotonic regression, temperature scaling, vector and matrix scaling, beta calibration

name: Conformal prediction
positive_test: produces sets or intervals with a finite-sample coverage guarantee under exchangeability
negative_test: producing a point probability with no coverage guarantee
examples: split conformal, full conformal, CQR, conformal risk control, adaptive conformal

name: Ensemble-based uncertainty
positive_test: estimates uncertainty from disagreement across independently trained or sampled models
negative_test: estimating from one model's output distribution
examples: deep ensembles, snapshot ensembles, batch ensembles, hyper-ensembles

name: Approximate Bayesian neural inference
positive_test: approximates a posterior over parameters and marginalises predictions over it
examples: Laplace approximation, Bayes-by-backprop, MC dropout, SWAG, SGLD posteriors

name: Out-of-distribution and selective prediction
positive_test: scores whether an input is outside the training distribution and may abstain
examples: max-softmax baseline, ODIN, Mahalanobis score, energy-based OOD, selective prediction

name: Test-time adaptation
characteristic: what is updated at test time
positive_test: updates the model or its statistics using unlabelled test data during deployment
negative_test: adapting with labelled target data before deployment
examples: TENT, TTT, SHOT
notes: adapting at test time is a property of the method, not its use

name: Normalisation-statistic adaptation
positive_test: recomputes normalisation statistics on test batches, updating no weights
negative_test: updating weights by an optimisation step
examples: BN-statistic adaptation, DUA, prediction-time BN

name: Entropy-minimisation adaptation
positive_test: takes gradient steps on the entropy or a confidence surrogate of test predictions
negative_test: taking steps on a self-supervised auxiliary loss
examples: TENT, EATA, SAR, CoTTA, RoTTA

name: Self-supervised test-time training
positive_test: takes gradient steps on an auxiliary self-supervised loss computed on the test input
negative_test: using the task head's own entropy
examples: TTT, TTT-MAE, MEMO, TTT-layers

name: Prototype and classifier-only adaptation
positive_test: re-estimates class prototypes or the classifier head from test features
examples: SHOT, T3A, prototype refinement

name: Inference-time aggregation
characteristic: over what the predictions are combined
positive_test: combines several models' or several runs' predictions into one output
examples: voting, averaging, stacking, Bayesian model averaging, mixture-of-experts routing at inference

name: Attribution and interpretation
characteristic: what the explanation is computed from
positive_test: produces an explanation of a trained model's behaviour as an output
examples: Grad-CAM, SHAP, activation patching
notes: an explanation is an output, so the participant rule admits this

name: Gradient-based attribution
positive_test: attributes using gradients or gradient paths through the network
negative_test: attributing by perturbing inputs and refitting a surrogate
examples: saliency maps, Grad-CAM, integrated gradients, SmoothGrad, GradientSHAP

name: Perturbation-based attribution
positive_test: attributes by measuring output change under input occlusion or resampling
examples: LIME, SHAP, occlusion, permutation importance, ablation studies

name: Probing and representation analysis
positive_test: fits or compares a simple readout on frozen internal representations
examples: linear probing, CKA, SVCCA, causal tracing, activation patching

name: Feature dictionary learning
positive_test: fits an overcomplete sparse basis over activations to name internal features
examples: sparse autoencoders, dictionary learning on activations, transcoders

name: Post-processing fairness adjustment
positive_test: adjusts thresholds or outputs per group on a trained model
examples: equalized-odds post-processing, reject-option classification, group-wise thresholds

name: Representation-based counterfactual estimation
positive_test: learns a representation balancing treated and control groups and predicts both potential outcomes
negative_test: using a fixed propensity model with no learned representation
examples: TARNet, CFR/IPM-balanced representations, Dragonnet, CEVAE, GANITE
